Two components: a three-line REFRAIN repeated six times verbatim (حكم ومباراة / كرة صفارة / لعب وإثارة في الملعب فانتظروا الشارة), monorhyming on -aara across مباراة صفارة إثارة الشارة; and a two-line VERSE sung twice (أجمل أوقاتي هي حين أمارس كرة اليد / هي حلم حياتي فيها اللعب وفيها الجد), rhyming on -ad with internal rhyme -aatii at the caesura. Layout is R R V V R R R R. This is verse, not running prose, and not a drill, table, list or MCQ.
law: THE PRINTED LINE IS THE UNIT. The source layout is fully preserved here (21 line breaks for 88 words), so the typesetting already encodes the metrical segmentation and every <NL> boundary plus the final token is forced-correct; those 22 give the backbone. Inside a line I cut only at a genuine SENTENCE juncture. I deliberately do NOT apply my K1 hemistich law in this document: the caesuras of the verse couplet fall after أوقاتي / حياتي (proved by the internal rhyme -aatii), and cutting there would strand a bare subject NP and orphan the subordinator حين, which my rule 6 forbids outright. Hemistich mode being impossible on the verse lines, the annotator must be working in sentence mode, and sentence mode is therefore what I apply to the refrain as well. Under sentence mode exactly one intra-line juncture exists in this text: the clause-initial ف of the imperative فانتظروا, which separates the complete verbless nominal sentence لعب وإثارة في الملعب from the imperative sentence فانتظروا الشارة. That juncture recurs identically six times and is cut all six times. Repeated identical text gets identical treatment.
reasoning: Five internal sites; one of them decides 6 of the 28 boundaries and is argued at length. (1) SITE 'حكم ومباراة' @0. The internal و joins two bare nouns (a referee and a match) with no predication of its own, so it is bare-noun و under the conjunct-weight test (doctrine section 0 and the connective table). NO CUT, hi confidence. Token 1 is a forced boundary anyway. (2) SITE 'كرة صفارة' @3. Two bare nouns in asyndeton, structurally the same phrase as حكم ومباراة with the و elided for meter. Two siblings is not a list: my I4 detector wants three or four parallel siblings before declaring one, and H5 tells me to be conservative about splitting within a run of bare NPs. Reading it as a two-item list would also contradict the fact that its twin line joins the same kind of pair with و and is undisputedly one unit. NO CUT, hi. (3) SITE 'أجمل أوقاتي هي حين أمارس كرة اليد' (7 tokens). No cut is available: هي is a copular damir al-fasl binding أجمل أوقاتي to its khabar, and حين is a tight subordinator whose complement is أمارس كرة اليد, so a cut after حين strands a dangling subordinator (rule 6: never cut after حتى / إلى أن / لأن and their class). ONE UNIT, hi. THIS IS THE DIAGNOSTIC LINE FOR THE WHOLE DOCUMENT: it is 7 tokens, longer than the 6-token refrain line, and it is a single unit, which removes any length-based pressure to split shorter lines; and because its metrical caesura (after أوقاتي, matched by حياتي in the sister line, internal rhyme -aatii) is grammatically uncuttable, hemistich segmentation cannot be what the annotator is doing here. That inference is what puts me in sentence mode for the rest of the document. (4) SITE 'هي حلم حياتي فيها اللعب وفيها الجد' (7 tokens). Two candidates. @36 is the asyndetic joint هي حلم حياتي || فيها اللعب وفيها الجد; @38 is before وفيها الجد. @38 is the tempting one, because فيها اللعب and وفيها الجد are isometric parallel predications each with its own PP frame and subject, and B2 says parallel enumerative clauses each get their own unit and that parallelism defeats the short-tail rule. I decline both cuts. وفيها الجد is a 2-token antithetical completion (لعب against جد) that lands on the line's rhyme word; the pair is one balanced predicate rather than an enumeration of the B2 kind, which had five members in expository prose; and decisively, this line is the second half of a couplet whose first line is unambiguously ONE unit at 7 tokens, so a couplet segmented 1 unit against 2 or 3 would be incoherent. @36 falls to the same couplet-symmetry argument plus the printed-line default. NO CUTS, but this is my weakest no-cut and @38 is my flagged risk on this document. (5) THE DECIDING SITE: 'لعب وإثارة في الملعب فانتظروا الشارة', six verbatim occurrences at 6-11, 19-24, 64-69, 77-82, 90-95, 103-108. This 6-token line is three times the length of the two 2-token refrain lines above it, which is the classic signature of two units run together. Three readings. (a) No internal cut, trust the printed line. (b) Cut @7 after وإثارة on metrical grounds: the refrain monorhymes on -aara, وإثارة is a rhyme word and الملعب is not, and حكم ومباراة / كرة صفارة / لعب وإثارة would then be three isometric roughly-6-syllable nominal siblings, which my checklist item 3 and B2/E1 parallelism rules would force apart. (c) Cut @9 after الملعب, immediately before the ف-imperative. I TAKE (c). Against (b): the rhyme argument dissolves once I notice that the PRINTED LINES ALREADY END ON THE RHYME (مباراة, صفارة, الشارة), so the monorhyme scheme is satisfied by the layout and needs no rescue; وإثارة is therefore ordinary tasrii/internal rhyme, not a unit-final rhyme. And (b) would leave لعب وإثارة as a bare mubtada with its khabar في الملعب amputated, which sentence mode forbids. I also rejected the three-way split لعب وإثارة || في الملعب || فانتظروا الشارة, attractive because it would make all five refrain units exactly 2 tokens, because a bare prepositional phrase is not a sentence unit and it too breaks the rhyme. For (c): لعب وإثارة في الملعب is a complete verbless nominal sentence (mubtada plus khabar-PP), and فانتظروا الشارة is an imperative addressed to the audience, a mood shift plus direct address. Two independent doctrine rules converge on exactly this token: clause-initial ف = CUT, near-absolute (B1, F3, connective table), and C4's hard-won lesson that the boundary goes immediately BEFORE the imperative (my وتصوروا failure, where I cut exactly one clause late). Against (a): my standing calibration is 7:1 under-segmentation, checklist rule 4 makes CUT the default that I must actively argue against, and K1 establishes that in this corpus verse lines do get cut internally (حمض سموم غبار || كونت مطرا, where gold split a single syntactic sentence). Because the refrain is verbatim-identical six times, all six occurrences receive the identical verdict; this is one judgement worth six boundaries, which is why I litigated it rather than guessing.
